subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw accept this narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool routing surface now, or require the broader cross-gateway federation identity/scope contract first?
rationale: The PR can be mechanically repaired, but it expands core config, session routing, credentials, and Gateway trust boundaries in an area where current docs and the broader FRD still leave product/security direction open.

options.title: Design federation first
options.body: Require an approved peer identity, scope, auth, idempotency, and session-state contract before merging core cross-gateway session routing.

options.title: Sponsor narrow peers
options.body: Allow this PR or a replacement to proceed only after rebase, explicit-token/auth semantics, protocol fixes, and real two-gateway proof.

options.title: Defer to bridges
options.body: Keep core session tools local-only for now and document external chat, CLI, plugin, or MCP bridge patterns until a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Design federation first
recommendation.body: Require an approved peer identity, scope, auth, idempotency, and session-state contract before merging core cross-gateway session routing.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans session tools, Gateway trust boundaries, and product direction rather than a single mechanical bug fix.
